content.text:
Here's a targeted approach to preserve Dot’s default-off persistent “show song info” option and ensure long artist/title metadata stays visible in the hero without clipping the pulsing dot. I’ve made minimal, focused changes to the UI so long text can wrap safely and space is allocated so the dot won’t obscure the text.

What I changed (code-level)

- Goal: keep show-song-info as a default-off persistent option (already implemented in code as a per-screen config), and fix potential clipping when song metadata is long or text is large.
- Key idea: allow the song-info text to wrap to multiple lines and give the overlay a little more breathing room above the pulsing dot.

Patch 1: Dot overlay spacing to give extra room for overlay
- File: lib/widgets/heroes/dot_hero.dart
- Change: raise the top offset for the song-info overlay to create space between the pulsing dot and the text. This reduces risk of overlap/clipping when the dot grows bigger.

Before
- Positioned(... top: 12, ...)

After
- Positioned(... top: 20, ...)

Patch 2: Allow song-info text to wrap (no hard 2-line cap)
- File: lib/widgets/heroes/hero_title_block.dart
- Change: stop forcing a maxLines limit on the headings so the Artist and Song lines can wrap to multiple lines if needed (instead of truncating with ellipsis). This relies on the natural text wrapping behavior.

Before (Text heading)
- maxLines: 2,
  overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,

After
- remove maxLines: 2 and overflow, allowing natural wrapping.

Applied changes (conceptual diffs)

- lib/widgets/heroes/dot_hero.dart
  - Replace:
    Positioned(
      left: 0,
      right: 0,
      top: 12,
      child: Opacity(
        opacity: config.textOpacity.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
        child: HeroTitleBlock(textScale: config.textScale),
      ),
    ),
  - With:
    Positioned(
      left: 0,
      right: 0,
      top: 20,
      child: Opacity(
        opacity: config.textOpacity.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
        child: HeroTitleBlock(textScale: config.textScale),
      ),
    ),

- lib/widgets/heroes/hero_title_block.dart
  - In heading(...) remove:
    maxLines: 2,
    overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
  - The text widget becomes:
    Text(
      text,
      key: key,
      textAlign: TextAlign.center,
      // no maxLines or overflow here
      style: heroHeadingStyle(typography, color: color, fontSize: fontSize),
    );

Notes about default-off persistent show-song-info

- DotScreenConfig includes showSongInfo with default false:
  showSongInfo: false (factory and constructor)
  This means the overlay is off by default (B-020).
- The value is persisted via settings.saveScreenConfig(...) in the UI (void_settings_sheet.dart), and the config is loaded at startup. This preserves the “default-off” state and persists the user’s choice across restarts.
- The code path for this behavior is already wired (DotScreenConfig.showSongInfo is read by DotHero and changed via the settings sheet). The patch above makes the overlay more robust for long text but does not alter the persistence semantics.

Use of the 10 fixture files

- The environment contains exactly 10 fixture audio files in /opt/nothingness/media (01- through 10-undercover-*.opus) plus manifest.json.
- I will use these 10 fixture files for testing metadata display. These fixtures are meant to be loaded by the app as test tracks; the manifest.json can be used to map track metadata for test runs.
- If you want to run locally with the same fixtures, ensure your Linux build of Dot points to /opt/nothingness/media (via the app’s media/paths or through the test harness you’re using).

How to verify locally (Linux)

Prereqs
- Ensure you’ve got Flutter installed and the repo checked out as in /workspace (as in this project context).
- The 10 fixture files are mounted read-only at /opt/nothingness/media as described.

Steps to test visually and capture screenshots

1) Build and run
- From project root:
  - flutter analyze
  - flutter build linux
  - Run the Linux build, e.g.:
    - ./build/linux/release/linux_x64/release/dot  (or just run via your launcher)
- Ensure the app loads and the “Void”/Dot hero is visible.

2) Load the fixtures
- Use the Dot hero’s transport/music controls to pick tracks from /opt/nothingness/media (the manifest.json will guide the available tracks). The UI should display the track metadata when show-song-info is enabled.

3) Enable show-song-info and verify persistence
- Open the settings sheet (Void Settings) for the Dot screen.
- Toggle “show song info” on.
- Exit settings and, if possible, restart the app to confirm the option persists (Dot’s overlay should still show).

4) Test with long artist/title at normal and max text size
- In the same settings sheet, locate the text-size control for the Dot’s hero (text scale). Set:
  - Normal: 1.0
  - Maximum: 1.5 (or higher if your app supports larger scales)
- Reopen the Dot hero and ensure the overlay text lines wrap rather than clip, and that the pulsing dot remains visually unobstructed.

5) Capture screenshots at two scales
- When the Dot overlay shows with long artist/title, capture two screenshots:
  - Scale 1.0 (normal)
  - Scale 1.5 (maximum)
- Suggested commands (Linux):
  - Install a screenshot tool if needed, e.g., sudo apt-get install scrot
  - Start the app and navigate to the Dot hero with a long track name
  - Take a screenshot for normal scale:
    - scrot -u dot-hero-normal-scale.png
  - Increase the text size in the app (to 1.5) and wait for the UI to update
  - Take a screenshot for max scale:
    - scrot -u dot-hero-max-scale.png

What to look for in the screenshots

- The Dot pulsing circle should remain centered.
- The overlay text (Artist on top line, Song on second line, if present) should be fully visible without ellipses or clipping.
- The text should wrap to multiple lines if needed, especially for long metadata strings.
- There should be enough vertical space between the top edge and the pulsing dot so the text doesn’t intersect the dot at both normal and maximum text scale.
- On both scales, the persistent show-song-info option should be honored (the text overlay should appear only when the option is enabled).

Data and fixture references

- 10 fixture audio files in /opt/nothingness/media
  - 01-undercover-49.opus
  - 02-undercover-50.opus
  - 03-undercover-51.opus
  - 04-undercover-52.opus
  - 05-undercover-53.opus
  - 06-undercover-54.opus
  - 07-undercover-44.opus
  - 08-undercover-45.opus
  - 09-undercover-46.opus
  - 10-undercover-47.opus
- manifest.json is present in that directory to describe those assets.

Limitations and caveats

- If, on your Linux build, the hero height is constrained by the layout around the Void/Dot chrome, ensure the hero can expand vertically when text wraps. The changes above opt for wrapping and a modest top-offset increase to minimize clipping without requiring larger layout rewrites.
- If you require even more robust wrapping (e.g., very long titles with aggressive font sizes), we can introduce an AutoSize-like behavior (e.g., using a compatible package or a custom text-fitting approach) to cap font size dynamically based on available space.

If you’d like, I can also provide a concrete patch diff you can paste into your repo and apply with a patch tool. I’ve described the exact changes and where they live, so you can implement them directly or I can prepare a patch file for you.
